findings.reason: the plan's own every-instance rule requires the full caller census, and both omitted sites are load-bearing — the dispatch grant is what makes a review worker's deliverable writable and the CLI verb answers "where is this record" for an outside consumer, so an unclassified caller can keep a stale root or a grant that no longer matches where records live.
findings.text: the plan's §3 Reads row names review_store_root's further direct callers as recovery.py, reports.py and runs.py, but the same census also finds dispatch.py (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1948, :4684, :4734, each passing review_store_root() as review_store_directory for sandbox_write_roots) and cli.py (reckon/cli.py:5527, the `reckon path --kind reviews` verb that resolves and prints the store root)

reuse_search-1.reason: acted on in v12: the census now names the dispatch.py sandbox write roots and the cli.py path verb, which the read-side node classifies with the other callers

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is added; the read-order complexity is pushed behind the existing resolver stored_record (reckon/crew/review.py:1696), through which the four readers are routed, so the surface does not spread.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan names the owners to extend (review_path in reckon/crew/review.py:1242, plan_review_path in reckon/crew/plan_review.py:349, stored_record, store_delivered_reviews) instead of forking placement, path resolution or state reading.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §3 states no MCP tool, view, view argument or server route is added, §4 states no view is added, §5 is a script rather than a CLI option and its store guard is a check inside the existing writers and not a new refusal family, so each section accounts for its surface in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the machinery this store extends (review_store_root, stored_record, store_delivered_reviews, _commit_state_write, the object-store write in recovery.py, and scripts/import_runs_into_store.py) but its census of review_store_root's direct callers omits dispatch.py and cli.py.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every proposed layer extends an existing owner (review_path, plan_review_path, store_delivered_reviews, _commit_state_write) rather than wrapping it, and the one new script takes import_runs_into_store.py's contract because its source and target genuinely differ.
